title: Christ and the New Covenant: The Messianic Message of the Book of Mormon
author: Jeffrey R. Holland
target_audience: Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
Religious scholars examining the Book of Mormon
Individuals interested in Christ-centered scripture study
core_themes: The centrality of Jesus Christ in the Book of Mormon
Covenant theology and the relationship between God and His children
The role of the Book of Mormon in modern Christianity
Faith, redemption, and spiritual transformation through Christ
primary_purpose: To explore and illuminate the profound Christ-centered teachings and Messianic prophecies contained within the Book of Mormon, providing doctrinal insights and spiritual encouragement for readers seeking a deeper understanding of Jesus Christ’s roles and mission according to Latter-day Saint scripture.

structure_format.narrative_style: Devotional, analytical, and scholarly with pastoral reflection
structure_format.organization: Arranged by topics and key figures, with chapters focusing on the teachings and prophecies about Christ in the Book of Mormon
features: Cross-referencing with Biblical and Latter-day Saint sources

key_concepts_lessons: The Book of Mormon is fundamentally a testimony of Jesus Christ.
The covenants made with God’s people are fulfilled through Christ.
Prophets in the Book of Mormon bore clear and direct witness of the Messiah years before His birth.
The doctrines of atonement, resurrection, and redemption are integral and explicitly taught in the Book of Mormon.
The Book of Mormon restores and clarifies essential Christian doctrines lost or obscured in other traditions.
Personal conversion and commitment are at the heart of covenantal teachings.
notable_features: Focus on Messianic prophecies in Latter-day Saint scripture
Combination of doctrinal analysis and devotional writing
Use of personal testimony from a high-ranking LDS Church leader
Accessible to both lay readers and scholars
Includes detailed scripture references and quotations
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of renewed interest in the Book of Mormon within Latter-day Saint communities, the book reflects a broader emphasis on Christ-centered teachings in LDS discourse of the late 20th century. Jeffrey R. Holland’s position as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles lends official perspective and church authority to the analysis.
reception_impact: Well received among Latter-day Saint readers for its clarity, depth, and spiritual insight
Widely used as a reference for talks, lessons, and gospel study
Appreciated for strengthening faith in Jesus Christ and reinforcing the Book of Mormon’s relevance
Cited in scholarly discussions on LDS Christology
Recognized for its contribution to devotional literature within the LDS tradition
comparable_titles: Jesus the Christ by James E. Talmage
Christ and the Everlasting Gospel by Tad R. Callister
The Book of Mormon: Another Testament of Jesus Christ by various commentators
Understanding the Book of Mormon by Grant Hardy
